I will keep my land in the same basic pattern that fits my experience and labor: 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 10 mu in cotton. I have farmed a long time, my household is small, and I have well irrigation, so I will stay with a steady plan I know I can manage myself. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen first and then a topdressing, and irrigate a few times because stable wheat yield matters to me. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same 10 mu because that rotation suits my land and gives me dependable grain output. I will fertilize maize a little heavier on nitrogen and keep irrigation ready for the key growth stages. For cotton, I will plant hybrid seed on the other 10 mu because it gives me better boll setting and yield than old seed in normal years. I will use moderate fertilizer, irrigate several times from squaring to boll filling, and spray when insects and disease pressure show up. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on 20 mu and fits my usual way of working.
